sim.explain.pwd: pwd shows the folder you are in.
sim.explain.ls: ls lists the files in this folder.
sim.explain.lsAll: ls -a also shows hidden files, like .git.
sim.explain.cat: cat shows what is inside a file.
sim.explain.echoAppend: You added a line to the end of {file}.
sim.explain.rm: You deleted {name}. Git did not help here.
sim.explain.help: These are the commands you can try here.
sim.explain.version: Git is installed. This is its version.
sim.explain.helpTopic: This is the help page for git {cmd}.
sim.explain.usage: -h shows a short help for git {cmd}.
sim.explain.configList: This lists all your Git settings.
sim.explain.configSetGlobal: Saved {key} for every project on this computer.
sim.explain.reinit: This folder was already a repo. Nothing was lost.
sim.explain.init: Git now watches this folder. It is a repo on branch {branch}.
sim.explain.initMaster: Git now watches this folder. Tip: set init.defaultBranch to main.
sim.explain.status: Green = in the box. Red = not in the box yet.
sim.explain.statusClean: Everything is saved. Nothing new to commit.
sim.explain.statusShort: Short view: left letter = the box, right letter = your folder.
sim.explain.addMany: You put {count} files in the box.
sim.explain.addNoop: Those changes were already in the box.
sim.explain.patchStart: Git shows one piece of change. Type y to take it, n to skip.
sim.explain.patchDone: Only the pieces you picked are in the box.
sim.explain.patchHelp: y = take it. n = skip it. q = stop.
sim.explain.amend: You replaced the last commit with a fixed one.
sim.explain.commitFirst: Your first save point! Git gave it the id {hash}.
sim.explain.commit: Saved! Git took a photo of the box: {hash}.
sim.explain.gitRm: Deleted {file} and told Git to stop tracking it.
sim.explain.gitRmCached: Git stops tracking {file}. The file stays in your folder.
sim.explain.mv: Renamed {from} to {to}. Git knows it moved.
sim.explain.logOneline: Your save points, newest first. One line each.
sim.explain.show: This shows what changed in commit {hash}.
sim.explain.diff.working: Red lines were removed. Green lines are new. Not in the box yet.
sim.explain.diff.staged: These changes are in the box, ready to commit.
sim.explain.diff.commits: What changed between these two commits.
sim.explain.reflog: Every place HEAD has been. Your safety net.
sim.explain.branch: The star shows where you are.
sim.explain.restoreBoth: {file} is back to the last commit, in the box and folder.
sim.explain.restoreStaged: You took {file} out of the box. Your change is still there.
sim.explain.restore: {file} is back to its saved version. The change is gone.
sim.explain.resetPath: You took {file} out of the box.
sim.explain.resetSoft: The branch moved back. Your changes wait in the box.
sim.explain.resetMixed: The branch moved back. Your changes are in your folder.
sim.explain.resetHard: Everything went back to {hash}. Unsaved changes were wiped.
sim.explain.revert: A new commit undoes {hash}. History stays safe.
sim.explain.detached: HEAD now points at {hash}, not a branch. Look around safely.
sim.explain.checkoutFile: {file} is back to the version in the box.
sim.explain.cleanDry: Just a preview. Nothing was deleted yet.
sim.explain.cleanForce: Deleted {count} untracked items. Git can't bring them back.
sim.err.notARepo: This folder is not a repo yet. Try git init, or cd into your project.
sim.err.lsOption: Here, try just ls or ls -a.
sim.err.noSuchPath: There is no {path} here. Try ls to see what exists.
sim.err.notADir: {path} is a file, not a folder.
sim.err.noManual: Git has no help page called {cmd}. Check the spelling.
sim.err.badOption: Git doesn't know the option {option}. Check the spelling.
sim.err.configKey: Settings look like section.name, for example user.name.
sim.err.configNeedsGlobal: You are not in a repo. Add --global to save it for everything.
sim.err.addNothing: Tell Git what to add. For example: git add index.html
sim.err.pathspec: No file called {path} here. Try ls or git status.
sim.err.addIgnored: {path} is in .gitignore, so Git skips it. That's usually good!
sim.err.nothingToAmend: There is no commit to fix yet. Make a commit first.
sim.err.needMessage: Add a message with -m. For example: git commit -m "Add home page"
sim.err.emptyMessage: Your message is empty. Say what you changed.
sim.err.noIdentity: Git needs your name and email first. Use git config --global.
sim.err.nothingStaged: The box is empty. Use git add first, then commit.
sim.err.nothingToCommit: Nothing changed since your last save point.
sim.err.rmPathspec: Git isn't tracking {path}. Check the name with git status.
sim.err.rmNeedR: That is a folder. Add -r to remove a folder.
sim.err.rmStaged: That file has changes in the box. Git stops you, to keep work safe.
sim.err.rmLocal: That file has unsaved changes. Git stops you, to keep work safe.
sim.err.mvBadSource: There is no {path} to move. Check the name.
sim.err.mvNotTracked: Git isn't tracking {path} yet. Use git add first.
sim.err.mvDestExists: A file with that new name already exists.
sim.err.badRevision: Git can't find {rev}. Try git log --oneline to see commits.
sim.err.noCommits: No commits yet. Make your first commit, then look back.
sim.explain.catFileType.blob: {name} is a blob: the content of one file.
sim.explain.catFileType.tree: {name} is a tree: a list of files and folders.
sim.explain.catFileType.commit: {name} is a commit: a snapshot with a message.
sim.explain.catFileType.tag: {name} is a tag object: a label with its own message.
sim.explain.catFilePretty.blob: That is the file content, stored as a blob.
sim.explain.catFilePretty.tree: A tree lists files (blobs) and folders (trees) with their ids.
sim.explain.catFilePretty.commit: A commit points to one tree, its parent, and who made it.
sim.explain.catFilePretty.tag: An annotated tag points to a commit and keeps a message.
sim.explain.catFileExists: {name} exists. -e only answers yes or no.
sim.explain.hashObject: That is the id Git gives this content. Same content, same id.
sim.explain.hashObjectWrite: -w also saved the content in Git as a blob.
sim.explain.lsTree: ls-tree lists one tree. Files are blobs, folders are trees.
sim.explain.lsTreeRecursive: -r goes into every folder and lists every file.
sim.explain.revParse: rev-parse turns a name like {rev} into a full id.
sim.explain.revParseShort: --short gives the short id you see in git log.
sim.explain.revParseAbbrevRef: --abbrev-ref HEAD shows the name of your branch.
sim.explain.revParseToplevel: That is the top folder of this repo.
sim.explain.revParseGitDir: That is where Git keeps the data for this folder.
sim.explain.showRef: show-ref lists every ref: a name that points to an id.
sim.explain.packRefsAll: All refs went into one file: .git/packed-refs.
sim.explain.catDotGit: Refs are tiny text files. HEAD names a branch or an id.
sim.explain.lsRefs: Each file here is one ref. It holds one commit id.
sim.explain.grep: git grep searched your tracked files for {pattern}.
sim.explain.grepRev: git grep searched the files as they were at {rev}.
sim.explain.grepNone: No line has {pattern}. Nothing found is fine.
sim.explain.blame: blame shows who last changed each line of {file}.
sim.explain.shortlog: shortlog groups the commits by author.
sim.explain.shortlogSummary: -s counts commits per author. -n puts the biggest first.
sim.explain.bisectStart: Bisect started. Now mark one good and one bad commit.
sim.explain.bisectTest: Git checked out {hash} for you. Test it, then say good or bad.
sim.explain.bisectMark.bad: {hash} is bad. Now mark a good commit.
sim.explain.bisectMark.good: {hash} is good. Now mark a bad commit.
sim.explain.bisectSkip: Skipped. Git will pick another commit to test.
sim.explain.bisectFound: Found it! {hash} ({message}) is the first bad commit.
sim.explain.bisectRunFound: The script tested each commit. {hash} ({message}) broke it.
sim.explain.bisectOnlySkipped: Only skipped commits are left. Git can't narrow it down more.
sim.explain.bisectReset: Bisect is over. You are back on {branch}.
sim.explain.bisectLog: The bisect log: every mark you made, in order.
sim.explain.bisectNotBisecting: No bisect is running, so there is nothing to reset.
sim.explain.alias: git {alias} is your alias. It ran {cmd}.
sim.explain.aliasHelp: --help on an alias shows what it stands for.
sim.explain.aliasShell: This alias runs a terminal command: {cmd}
sim.explain.script: {file} ended with exit code {code}. 0 means good.
sim.explain.grepFound: grep found {pattern}. That is exit code 0.
sim.explain.grepNotFound: grep found no {pattern}. That is exit code 1.
sim.explain.testTrue: The test is true. That is exit code 0.
sim.explain.testFalse: The test is false. That is exit code 1.
sim.explain.worktreeAdd: New working folder {path} on branch {branch}. Same repo inside.
sim.explain.worktreeList: Every working folder of this repo, with its branch.
sim.explain.worktreeRemove: The folder {path} is gone. Its branch and commits stay.
sim.explain.worktreePrune: Git forgot worktrees whose folders were deleted.
sim.explain.worktreeNotInSim: This practice terminal doesn't run git worktree {sub}.
sim.explain.notInSim.rerere: rerere remembers how you fixed a conflict. The lesson shows it.
sim.explain.notInSim.range-diff: range-diff compares two versions of a branch. The lesson shows it.
sim.explain.notInSim.submodule: A submodule puts one repo inside another. The lesson shows it.
sim.explain.notInSim.subtree: subtree copies another repo into a folder. The lesson shows it.
sim.explain.notInSim.lfs: Git LFS keeps big files outside the repo. The lesson shows it.
sim.explain.notInSim.sparse-checkout: sparse-checkout fills in only some folders. The lesson shows it.
sim.explain.notInSim.gc: gc packs loose objects to save space. The lesson shows it.
sim.explain.notInSim.maintenance: maintenance tidies a repo in the background. The lesson shows it.
sim.explain.notInSim.count-objects: count-objects counts what Git stored. The lesson shows it.
sim.explain.notInSim.repack: repack rebuilds packfiles. The lesson shows it.
sim.explain.notInSim.prune: prune deletes objects nothing points to. The lesson shows it.
sim.explain.notInSim.fsck: fsck checks that every object is healthy. The lesson shows it.
sim.explain.notInSim.whatchanged: whatchanged is old. Use git log instead.
sim.explain.notInSim.hook: Hooks are scripts Git runs for you. The lesson shows them.
sim.explain.notInSim.refs: git refs works on how refs are stored. The lesson shows it.

sim.err.badObject: Git has no object called {name}. Check the id or name.

sim.err.blameRange: That line range doesn't fit the file: {range}
sim.err.blameUsage: Give blame a file, like: git blame index.html

sim.err.hashObjectStdin: No pipes here. Give a file name instead.
sim.err.hashObjectUsage: Give it a file, like: git hash-object index.html
sim.err.lsTreeUsage: Give it a commit or tree, like: git ls-tree HEAD

sim.err.notTree: {name} is not a tree or a commit.

sim.err.objectNoPath: {path} is not there. Check the path with git ls-tree.

sim.err.shUsage: Run a script like this: sh test.sh
sim.err.showRefMissing: {ref} is not a ref. Use a full name like refs/heads/main.

detective.resultGood: The test passed. This commit is good.
detective.testFirst: Run the test first. Then you will know.

detective.almostGood: Almost! The test passed here, so this commit is good.
detective.found: Found it! {short} ({message}) is the first bad commit.
detective.success: You caught the bug in {n} tests.
detective.empty: This repo needs at least two commits.

sim.err.revertNeedCommit: Tell Git which commit to undo. For example: git revert HEAD
sim.err.revertMany: Undo one commit at a time here.
sim.err.revertDirty: Save or undo your current changes first. Then revert.

sim.err.switchUntracked: An untracked file is in the way. Move or delete it first.
sim.err.switchDirty: You have unsaved changes. Commit or restore them first.
sim.err.noPrevious: There is no previous place to go back to.
sim.err.switchNeedBranch: Tell Git where to go. For example: git switch main
sim.err.switchNeedsDetach: {rev} is a commit, not a branch. Add --detach to visit it.
sim.err.noSuchBranch: There is no branch called {branch}. Try git branch.
sim.err.cleanIgnored: Here we keep ignored files safe. Use -n or -f.
sim.err.cleanRequireForce: Git wants you to be sure. Use -n to preview, -f to delete.
sim.err.unknownGitDidYouMean: Hmm, Git doesn't know git {cmd}. Did you mean git {suggestion}?
sim.err.unknownGit: Hmm, Git doesn't know git {cmd}. Try git help.
sim.err.oneAtATime: Type one command at a time here.
sim.err.unclosedQuote: Close your quote with a matching ".
sim.err.redirectTarget: After > you need a file name.
sim.err.unknownCmdDidYouMean: Hmm, {cmd} isn't a command. Did you mean {suggestion}?
sim.err.unknownCmd: Hmm, {cmd} isn't a command here. Type help to see the list.
sim.explain.branchCreate: New branch {branch}! It is a sticky note on {hash}. You are still where you were.
sim.explain.branchCreateAt: New branch {branch}, stuck on {rev}. You did not move.
sim.explain.branchDelete: Removed the sticky note {branch}. Its commits are safe in main.
sim.explain.branchForceDelete: Removed {branch}, even with unmerged work. Only the reflog remembers it now.
sim.explain.branchMerged: These branches are already part of this one. Safe to delete.
sim.explain.branchNoMerged: These branches have work that is not merged here yet.
sim.explain.branchShowCurrent: This is the branch you are on.
sim.explain.branchAll: Red names are remote copies, like origin/main.
sim.explain.branchVV: In brackets: the upstream, and how far ahead or behind you are.
sim.explain.upstreamSet: {branch} now follows {upstream}. Push and pull know where to go.
sim.explain.upstreamUnset: {branch} no longer follows a remote branch.
sim.explain.switchCreate: You made {branch} and moved onto it in one step.
sim.explain.switchCreateAt: You made {branch} at {rev} and moved onto it.
sim.explain.switchCreateTrack: You made {branch} from {upstream}. It follows that remote branch.
sim.explain.mergeUpToDate: Nothing to do. You already have everything from {branch}.
sim.explain.mergeFastForward: Fast-forward! Your branch label just slid forward to {branch}.
sim.explain.mergeCommit: Git joined {branch} into yours with a new merge commit, {hash}.
sim.explain.mergeConflictOne: Conflict in {file}. Both sides changed the same lines. You choose.
sim.explain.mergeConflictMany: {count} files have conflicts. Fix each one, then git add it.
sim.explain.mergeAbort: Merge cancelled. Everything is back to how it was before.
sim.explain.mergeCommitDefault: No editor here, so Git used its default message: {message}
sim.explain.addResolvedAll: All conflicts are fixed. Now commit to finish.
sim.explain.addResolvedSome: Marked as fixed. Conflicted files left: {count}.
sim.explain.addResolvedMarkers: Careful! {file} still has <<<<<<< markers. Git trusts you anyway.
sim.explain.statusConflict: Red files have conflicts. Fix them, then git add each one.
sim.explain.statusMergeConflict: You are in the middle of a merge. Fix the red files first.
sim.explain.statusMergeReady: All fixed! Run git commit to finish the merge.
sim.explain.statusRebaseConflict: Rebase paused on a conflict. Fix it, git add, then continue.
sim.explain.statusPickConflict: Cherry-pick paused on a conflict. Fix it, git add, then continue.
sim.explain.statusAhead: You are ahead of {upstream} by {ahead}. Push to share your work.
sim.explain.statusBehind: {upstream} is ahead of you by {behind}. Pull to catch up.
sim.explain.statusDiverged: Both sides moved: {ahead} new here, {behind} new there.
sim.explain.stashPush: Your changes went into the stash drawer. The folder is clean now.
sim.explain.stashPushUntracked: Changes and new files went into the stash drawer.
sim.explain.stashNothing: Nothing to stash. Your folder is already clean.
sim.explain.stashList: Your stash drawer. The newest stash is at the top.
sim.explain.stashShow: This is what is inside that stash.
sim.explain.stashPop: Your changes are back, and that stash is gone from the drawer.
sim.explain.stashApply: Your changes are back. The stash stays in the drawer too.
sim.explain.stashClear: The stash drawer is empty now. Those changes are gone.
sim.explain.stashConflict: The stash clashed with {file}. Fix it. The stash is kept for you.
sim.explain.rebaseDone: Your commits now sit on top of the new base. Same changes, new ids.
sim.explain.rebaseUpToDate: {branch} already sits on top. Nothing to replay.
sim.explain.rebaseConflict: Rebase paused: {file} has a conflict. Fix it, git add, then continue.
sim.explain.rebaseAbort: Rebase cancelled. Your branch is back where it started.
sim.explain.rebaseQuit: Git stopped the rebase and left things as they are.
sim.explain.rebaseCommitted: Saved this step. Run git rebase --continue for the rest.
sim.explain.cherryPick: Copied commit {hash} onto your branch as a new commit.
sim.explain.cherryPickConflict: The copy clashed with {file}. Fix it, git add, then continue.
sim.explain.cherryPickEmpty: Nothing new to copy. Those changes are already here. Try --skip.
sim.explain.cherryPickAbort: Cherry-pick cancelled. Your branch is back to how it was.
sim.explain.cherryPickQuit: Git forgot the cherry-pick and left your files as they are.
sim.explain.tagCreate: Tag {tag} now marks {hash}. Tags never move.
sim.explain.tagAnnotated: Annotated tag {tag} on {hash}, with your name, date and message.
sim.explain.tagDelete: Tag {tag} removed. The commit is still there.
sim.explain.remoteList: These are your remotes: nicknames for online copies.
sim.explain.remoteV: Each remote and its web address, for fetch and for push.
sim.explain.remoteNone: No remotes yet. Add one with git remote add origin <url>.
sim.explain.remoteRemove: Removed the remote {remote}. The online copy is untouched.
sim.explain.remoteSetUrl: {remote} now points to a new address.
sim.explain.push: Sent your new commits to {remote}. GitHub now has them.
sim.explain.pushNewBranch: Sent {branch} to {remote}. It is a new branch there.
sim.explain.pushUpToDate: Nothing to send. {remote} already has everything.
sim.explain.pushForced: Forced {branch} on the remote. Its old commits were replaced.
sim.explain.fetch: Downloaded news from {remote}. Your own branches did not change.
sim.explain.fetchNoRemote: There is no remote to fetch from yet.
sim.explain.clone: Copied the whole project into {dir}. Its remote is called origin.
sim.explain.cloneEmpty: Cloned into {dir}. The project is empty, so make the first commit!

sim.err.branchExists: A branch called {branch} already exists. Pick another name.
sim.err.branchForceCurrent: You are on {branch}, so Git won't move it. Switch away first.
sim.err.branchBadStart: Git can't find {rev} to start from. Check git log --oneline.

sim.err.branchNotFound: There is no branch called {branch}. Try git branch.
sim.err.branchDeleteCurrent: You are standing on {branch}. Switch to another branch first.

sim.err.branchRenameDetached: You are not on a branch. Name the branch to rename.
sim.err.upstreamMissing: There is no {upstream} yet. Try git fetch, or push with -u.

sim.err.pathUnmerged: {path} has a conflict. Fix the file and git add it.

sim.err.mergeOne: Here, merge one branch at a time.
sim.err.mergeDirty: Your unsaved changes would be overwritten. Commit or stash them first.
sim.err.mergeUntracked: An untracked file is in the way. Move or delete it first.
sim.err.mergeFFOnly: The branches went different ways, so no fast-forward. Merge or rebase.

holes.instructions: Tap every risky line. Each one shows the attack and the fix.
holes.codeLabel: Workflow lines. Tap a line to check it.
holes.kind.selfHosted: Your own machine, open to all
holes.attackText.unpinned: A tag can move. If someone takes over the action, the same tag runs bad code. In March 2025, tags of tj-actions/changed-files were moved like this. Secrets leaked.
holes.attackText.writeAll: Every step gets every key. One bad step can push code or delete releases.
holes.attackText.prTargetCheckout: pull_request_target runs with your secrets and a write token. This line checks out the stranger's code and runs it with them.
holes.attackText.injection: Anyone can write an issue title. A title with quotes and a command becomes part of your script.
holes.attackText.secretEcho: Printing a secret puts it in the log. GitHub hides exact matches, but a changed copy slips through.
holes.attackText.selfHosted: Anyone can open a pull request on a public repo. Their code could run on your own machine.
holes.attackText.other: This line gives an attacker a way in.
holes.fixText.unpinned: Pin the full commit SHA. Keep the version in a comment. Let Dependabot update it.
holes.fixText.writeAll: Give only what the job needs, like contents: read.
holes.fixText.prTargetCheckout: Use pull_request for code from forks. It gets no secrets and a read-only token.
holes.fixText.injection: Put the value in an env variable. Use "$TITLE" in the script.
holes.fixText.secretEcho: Never print secrets. Pass them by env to the tool that needs them.
holes.fixText.selfHosted: Use GitHub-hosted runners on public repos.
holes.fixText.other: Change this line so it gives less away.
holes.hint.unpinned: Hint: look at the “uses:” lines. Which one has no full SHA?
holes.hint.writeAll: Hint: look at “permissions:”. How many keys does it give?
holes.hint.prTargetCheckout: Hint: which code does the checkout step fetch?
holes.hint.secretEcho: Hint: look for a secret inside an echo.
holes.hint.selfHosted: Hint: look at “runs-on:”. Whose machine is it?
holes.hint.other: Hint: one more line is risky.

linux.err.noFile: Almost! {name} doesn't exist here. Try ls to see the names.
linux.err.noExec: Almost! {name} has no x permission yet. Try chmod +x first.
linux.err.isDirRun: {name} is a folder, not a program.
linux.err.isDir: {name} is a folder. Try ls on it instead.
linux.err.readDenied: You may not read {name}. Check ls -l: who owns it?
linux.err.writeDenied: You may not write there. It belongs to someone else.
linux.err.cdMissing: Almost! There is no folder {path} here.
linux.err.cdNotDir: {path} is a file. cd only goes into folders.
linux.err.cdDenied: That folder is locked for you. Its owner didn't give you x.
linux.err.lsMissing: ls couldn't open {path}. Check the name, or who may read it.
linux.err.exists: {name} is already there. Pick another name, or use it.
linux.err.mkdirParent: The folder above is missing. mkdir -p makes it too.
linux.err.rmDir: {name} is a folder. rm -r removes folders (careful!).
linux.err.rmDenied: You may not delete {name}. The folder isn't yours.
linux.err.cpNeedsR: {name} is a folder. cp -r copies folders.
linux.err.badMode: Almost! {mode} isn't a mode. Try 755 or u+x.
linux.err.notOwner: Only the owner (or root) may change {name}'s permissions.
linux.err.chownRoot: Only root may give a file away. Try sudo.
linux.err.notSudoer: {user} may not use sudo on this server.
linux.err.sudoNotFound: sudo can't find a program called {name}.
linux.err.suPassword: root has no password here. Use sudo -i instead.
linux.err.passwdNoTyping: The practice server can't take passwords. On a real one, passwd asks twice.
linux.err.noProcess: No process has PID {pid}. Check ps first.
linux.err.killDenied: That process isn't yours. Only root may stop it.
linux.err.noJob: There is no such job. Try jobs to see them.
linux.err.startFailed: {name} didn't start. Check systemctl status {name} for the reason.
linux.err.journalNeedsRoot: Your user may not read the system log. Add sudo.
linux.err.curlResolve: No address for {host}. Check the name, or DNS.
linux.err.curlRefused: Nothing listens on {host} port {port}. Is the service running?
linux.err.curlTimeout: {host} port {port} never answered. A firewall may drop it.
linux.err.pingResolve: No address for {host}. Check the name.
linux.err.pingNoReply: {host} didn't answer. It may be down, or ping is blocked.
linux.err.cronBad: That crontab line has a mistake in its time fields.
linux.err.noEditor: No editor here. Write the jobs to a file, then: crontab {file}
linux.err.keyExists: That key file already exists. Pick another name with -f.
aws.iam.help.predict: Read the request and its policies. Will AWS say Allow or Deny?
aws.iam.help.edit: Change the pink line so AWS says {want}.
aws.iam.why.explicitDeny: {where} says Deny, and it fits. A Deny always wins.
aws.iam.why.scpNoAllow: The SCPs at {level} have no Allow for this. That means no.
aws.iam.why.scpAllows: Every SCP level has an Allow for this.
aws.iam.why.noResourcePolicy: This resource has no policy of its own.
aws.iam.why.resourceNoAllow: The resource policy doesn't allow this caller here.
aws.iam.why.resourceAllowsUser: {where} names this IAM user. In one account, that is enough.
aws.iam.why.resourceAllowsSession: {where} names this role session. In one account, that is enough.
aws.iam.why.resourceAllowsRole: {where} names the role. The fence still gets a say.
aws.iam.why.identityNotNeeded: Not needed: the resource policy already allows the role.
aws.iam.why.identityNoAllow: No identity policy allows this. No Allow means Deny.
aws.iam.why.noIdentityPolicy: This caller has no identity policy. No Allow means Deny.
aws.iam.why.boundaryNoAllow: The fence doesn't allow this. A fence can only limit.
aws.iam.final.denyExplicit: Deny. A Deny statement said no (explicit deny).
aws.iam.hint.deny: Look for a Deny that fits first. One Deny beats every Allow.
aws.iam.hint.scp: Check the SCPs. Every level must allow it.
aws.iam.hint.identity: Does any identity policy allow this exact action on this resource?
aws.iam.hint.boundary: Check the fence. It must allow it too.
aws.iam.hint.allow: No Deny fits, and every guard finds an Allow.
aws.iam.hint.resource: The resource policy names this caller. In one account, that is enough.
aws.iam.jsonError: That line doesn't read as JSON yet. Check the quotes and the comma.
aws.iam.issueCode.notObject: it must be one JSON object.
aws.iam.issueCode.needAction: each statement needs Action or NotAction.
aws.iam.issueCode.bothAction: use Action or NotAction, not both.
aws.iam.issueCode.needResource: each statement needs Resource or NotResource.
aws.iam.issueCode.bothResource: use Resource or NotResource, not both.
aws.iam.issueCode.actionFormat: an action looks like service:Action, like s3:GetObject.
aws.iam.issueCode.serviceWildcard: no wildcard in the service part of an ARN.
aws.iam.issueCode.arnFormat: a resource is an ARN (arn:aws:…) or *.
aws.iam.issueCode.principalNeeded: a resource policy names a Principal.
aws.iam.issueCode.principalNotAllowed: only resource policies have a Principal.
aws.iam.issueCode.principalType: this game knows IAM user, role and role session ARNs only.
aws.iam.issueCode.operator: this game doesn't know that condition operator.
aws.iam.issueCode.variable: this game doesn't fill in policy variables.
aws.iam.issueCode.unknownKey: this game doesn't know that field.
aws.iam.issueCode.ipv6: this game checks IPv4 addresses only.
aws.iam.forbid: That works, but it opens too much. Give a smaller key.
aws.subnet.help: Give each row of units its own block of addresses. Nothing may overlap.
aws.subnet.briefNeed: {tier}: {n}, one per zone, each with at least {need} usable addresses.
aws.subnet.empty: No subnet yet. Pick a size.
aws.subnet.err.tooBig: /{prefix} is too big. Subnets are /16 to /28.
aws.subnet.err.tooSmall: /{prefix} is too small. Subnets are /16 to /28.
aws.subnet.vpcErr.tooBig: /{prefix} is too big. A VPC is /16 to /28.
aws.subnet.vpcErr.tooSmall: /{prefix} is too small. A VPC is /16 to /28.
aws.subnet.vpcErr.forbidden: AWS doesn't allow {range} for a VPC.
aws.subnet.vpcErr.avoid172: Some AWS services use {range}. Pick another range to be safe.
aws.subnet.vpcErr.publicRange: This is a public range. Private ranges (10.x, 172.16–31.x, 192.168.x) are the usual pick.
aws.subnet.reserved: Which 5 addresses does AWS keep in {cidr}?
aws.subnet.noRoom: No free /{prefix} block is left in this VPC.
aws.subnet.done: Every row has its own road, and nothing overlaps.
aws.gate.help.sg: Set the door guard's rules. Only the right visitors get in.
aws.gate.help.nacl: Set the row gate's list. Right visitors in, their replies out.
aws.gate.help.both: Set both guards. Right visitors in, replies out, the rest kept out.
aws.gate.client: Its replies go back to ports {from}–{to}.
aws.gate.naclNote: Lowest number first. The first rule that fits decides. It remembers nothing, so replies need an Out rule.
aws.gate.sgNote: Allow rules only. It remembers who came in, so replies always go out.
aws.gate.sgOut: Out: all traffic (a new group starts this way).
aws.gate.noRules: No In rules yet: nothing gets in.
aws.gate.result.in: Got in, and the reply got out.
aws.gate.result.door: Stopped at the door: no rule lets it in.
aws.gate.result.gateOut: Got in, but the gate stopped the reply (rule {rule}).
aws.gate.result.replySometimes: Got in, but replies to ports {from}–{to} are stopped.
aws.gate.trace.stateful: Reply: the door remembers, so it may leave
aws.gate.badRule.duplicate: That rule number is taken. Pick another.
aws.gate.badRule.source: There is no group with that name here.
aws.gate.forbidOpen: Port {port} is open to the whole internet. Allow only trusted addresses.
aws.gate.done: The right visitors get in, and their replies get out.
aws.idle.help: One at a time: does it keep costing money while it sits idle?
aws.idle.billTitle: On the bill (costs even when idle)
aws.idle.cleanupNote: Delete these when you are done. Prices change, so check the official pages.
aws.idle.freeTier: Free tier rules change. Check the AWS Free Tier page.
aws.idle.done: You can spot what eats money while you sleep.
aws.idle.item.natGateway.name: NAT gateway with no traffic
aws.idle.item.natGateway.why: It is billed for every hour it exists, plus each GB it passes on.
aws.idle.item.elasticIpIdle.name: Elastic IP not attached to anything
aws.idle.item.elasticIpIdle.why: AWS charges for every public IPv4 address, in use or idle.
aws.idle.item.elasticIpStopped.name: Elastic IP on a stopped instance
aws.idle.item.elasticIpStopped.why: The instance rests, but its Elastic IP still costs money.
aws.idle.item.ebsDetached.name: EBS volume nobody uses
aws.idle.item.ebsDetached.why: A detached disk is still billed. Delete it to stop paying.
aws.idle.item.ebsOfStopped.name: Disk (EBS volume) of a stopped instance
aws.idle.item.ebsOfStopped.why: Stopping keeps the disks, and you pay to store them.
aws.idle.item.ebsSnapshot.name: Old EBS snapshot
aws.idle.item.ebsSnapshot.why: You pay to store snapshot data until you delete it.
aws.idle.item.loadBalancer.name: Load balancer with no visitors
aws.idle.item.loadBalancer.why: It is billed for each hour, or part of an hour, it runs.
aws.idle.item.rdsRunning.name: RDS database nobody queries
aws.idle.item.rdsRunning.why: A running database bills instance hours, busy or not.
aws.idle.item.rdsStopped.name: Stopped RDS database
aws.idle.item.rdsStopped.why: Storage and backups still cost. It also starts again by itself after 7 days.
aws.idle.item.eksCluster.name: EKS cluster with no apps
aws.idle.item.eksCluster.why: Every cluster has an hourly fee, even when empty.
aws.idle.item.interfaceEndpoint.name: Interface VPC endpoint
aws.idle.item.interfaceEndpoint.why: It is billed for each hour it exists, in each Availability Zone.
aws.idle.item.secret.name: Secret in Secrets Manager
aws.idle.item.secret.why: You pay for each secret you keep stored.
aws.idle.item.hostedZone.name: Route 53 hosted zone
aws.idle.item.hostedZone.why: Each hosted zone has a monthly charge.
aws.idle.item.s3Objects.name: S3 bucket full of old files
aws.idle.item.s3Objects.why: You pay to store the files, even if nobody reads them.
aws.idle.item.ecrImages.name: Old images in ECR
aws.idle.item.ecrImages.why: You pay for the image data stored in your repositories.
aws.idle.item.lambdaProvisioned.name: Lambda with provisioned concurrency
aws.idle.item.lambdaProvisioned.why: You pay for the ready capacity for as long as it is on.
aws.idle.item.vpc.name: An empty VPC
aws.idle.item.vpc.why: The VPC itself has no charge. Some parts inside it do.
aws.idle.item.securityGroup.name: Security group
aws.idle.item.securityGroup.why: There is no extra charge for security groups.
aws.idle.item.networkAcl.name: Network ACL
aws.idle.item.networkAcl.why: There is no extra charge for network ACLs.
aws.idle.item.internetGateway.name: Internet gateway
aws.idle.item.internetGateway.why: The gateway is free. Data that goes through it can cost.
aws.idle.item.gatewayEndpoint.name: Gateway VPC endpoint (S3 or DynamoDB)
aws.idle.item.gatewayEndpoint.why: Gateway endpoints have no hourly or data processing charge.
aws.idle.item.privateIp.name: Private IPv4 address (10.x, 172.16–31.x, 192.168.x)
aws.idle.item.privateIp.why: Private IPv4 addresses are not charged. Public ones are.
aws.idle.item.iam.name: IAM users, roles and policies
aws.idle.item.iam.why: IAM is free. You pay only for what they use.
aws.idle.item.ecsCluster.name: Empty ECS cluster
aws.idle.item.ecsCluster.why: ECS itself has no extra charge. You pay for what runs.
aws.idle.item.stoppedInstance.name: Stopped EC2 instance (its computing time)
aws.idle.item.stoppedInstance.why: No compute charge while it is stopped. Its disks still cost!
aws.idle.item.lambdaFunction.name: Lambda function nobody calls
aws.idle.item.lambdaFunction.why: Lambda bills per request and run time. No calls, no charge.

promql.help: Type a PromQL query and press Run. The table shows the answer at the eval time. The graph shows it over time.
promql.metrics: Metrics in this data (tap to add):
promql.evalHelp: Time 0 is when the data starts. The query looks back from the eval time.
promql.result.matrix: {n} series with their samples (a range vector) at {t}
promql.result.emptyHint: Check the metric name and labels. Or move the eval time.
promql.graph.title: Graph: the query at every step, 0 to {end}
promql.graph.label: Line graph of {n} series from 0 to {end}. The pink line marks the eval time, {t}.
promql.graph.matrix: A range vector is a list of samples, so it has no line. Wrap it in a function like rate() to graph it.
promql.graph.none: Nothing to draw: no series at any step.
promql.graph.many: Many series, so the lines are grey. Pick one below to light it up.
promql.err.wrongType: This spot needs a value of type {want}, but it got {got}.
promql.err.scalarCompare: Comparing two plain numbers needs the word bool, like 1 > bool 2.
promql.err.unknownFunction: There is no function called {name}. Check the spelling.
promql.err.unclosedParen: A bracket ( is never closed. Add a ) at the right place.
promql.err.unclosedBrace: A { is never closed. Add a } after the labels.
promql.err.unclosedBracket: A [ is never closed. Write the range like [5m].
promql.err.unexpected: Something here is in the wrong place. Look at the spot it names.
promql.err.unexpectedEnd: The query stops too early. Something is missing at the end.
promql.err.badNumber: That is not a number or a duration. Durations look like 30s, 5m or 1h.
promql.err.badDuration: That duration has the wrong units. Try 30s, 5m or 1h30m.
promql.err.rangeOnSelector: A range like [5m] can only follow a metric name and its labels.
promql.err.offsetBeforeRange: Put the range first, then offset: x[5m] offset 1m.
promql.err.zeroRange: A range must be longer than 0.
promql.err.emptySelector: Give the selector a metric name, or a label that must not be empty.
promql.err.badRegex: That regex is broken. Check its brackets and stars.
promql.err.argCount: {func} takes a different number of inputs.
promql.err.aggArgs: This aggregation takes a different number of inputs.
promql.err.aggNoArgs: Put something inside the brackets, like sum(up).
promql.err.boolPlace: bool only goes after a comparison like > or ==.
promql.err.setScalar: and, or and unless join two lists of series, not plain numbers.
promql.err.setGrouping: and, or and unless never take group_left or group_right.
promql.err.binaryTypes: Maths and comparisons work on numbers and instant vectors only.
promql.err.matchingScalar: on() and ignoring() only work between two lists of series.
promql.err.onAndGroup: A label can't be in on() and in group_left() at once.
promql.err.sameLabelset: Two answers ended up with the same labels. Keep a label that tells them apart.
promql.err.manyToMany: Several series on one side match the same group. Match on more labels.
promql.err.manyToOne: Many series match one. Add group_left (or group_right) to allow that.
promql.err.groupingUnique: group_left still gives two answers with the same labels. Match on more labels.
promql.err.unterminated: A quote is never closed. Add the closing quote.
promql.err.unaryType: A minus sign only works on numbers and instant vectors.
promql.err.offsetPlace: offset goes right after a metric selector or a range.
promql.err.atPlace: @ goes right after a metric selector or a range.
promql.err.syntax: Something in the query can't be read. Look at the spot it names.
promql.err.engineLimit: Real Prometheus can run this. This practice engine can't yet, sorry!
promql.err.rangeQueryType: A graph needs numbers at each step, not a range vector.
promql.err.template: This message template uses something the practice engine can't run.
promql.err.ruleResultType: An alert needs an instant vector or a number, not a range vector.
promql.err.alertSameLabelset: Two alerts got the same labels. Keep a label that tells them apart.
promql.err.recordSameLabelset: Two results got the same labels. Keep a label that tells them apart.
promql.err.generic: Something went wrong in this query.
promql.miss.typed: Try the query the task asks for.
promql.miss.type: The answer should be of type {want}, not {got}.
promql.miss.count: You got {got} series. The task wants {want}.
promql.miss.empty: No series came back. Check the name, the labels, and the time.
promql.miss.labelNames: Your series have the labels {got}. The task wants only {want}.
promql.miss.extraSeries: There are extra series, like {series}. Filter or sum them.
promql.alert.help: Build an alert rule from the blocks. The timeline shows when it would wait and when it would fire.
promql.alert.timeline: What the alert does over time
promql.alert.legend: Grey: quiet. Amber: pending (true, but waiting). Red: firing.
promql.alert.never: The expression never returned anything. The alert stays quiet the whole time.
promql.alert.done: The alert fires when it should, and only then.
promql.alert.changed: Rule changed. The timeline is updated.
promql.alertMiss.error: The rule has an error. Pick other blocks.
promql.alertMiss.neverFires: This rule never fires. The problem would go unseen.
promql.alertMiss.tooEarly: It fires at {at}. That is too early: a short blip would wake someone up.
promql.alertMiss.tooLate: It fires at {at}. That is too late: customers waited a long time.
promql.alertMiss.notFiringAt: At {at} it should be firing, but it isn't.
promql.alertMiss.firingAt: At {at} it is firing, but nothing is wrong then.
promql.alertMiss.flaps: {series} fires {n} separate times. That is flapping. Wait a little first.
promql.alertMiss.wrongTarget: It fires for {series}, which is not broken. Pick a sharper expression.
promql.alertMiss.labels: Add the label {label}, so the alert goes to the right people.
promql.alertMiss.annotation: Make the message use {text}, so people know what broke.
k9.shell.inside: You are inside node {node}. Type exit to go back to your laptop.
k9.danger.node: Careful: this changes {node} itself. On a real node, that is for real.
k9.fault.note.stopKubelet: Someone ran systemctl stop kubelet on a stall.
k9.fault.note.startKubelet: The kubelet on that stall started again.
k9.fault.note.breakStaticPod: Someone edited a manifest in the manager's office.
k9.explain.fault.stopKubelet: That stall's kubelet stopped. After 50 s the node shows NotReady.
k9.explain.fault.startKubelet: The kubelet runs again. The node turns Ready in a few seconds.
k9.explain.fault.breakStaticPod: A control-plane manifest changed. The kubelet notices it in a few seconds.
k9.explain.ssh: You are on {node} now. On kind, docker exec -it {node} bash does the same.
k9.explain.dockerExec: You opened a shell inside the kind node {node}. It is a Docker container.
k9.explain.sshOneCommand: Open the shell first: ssh {node}. Then type the command.
k9.explain.dockerOnlyExec: Here, docker only opens a node: docker exec -it dev-worker bash.
k9.explain.exit: You left {node}. You are back on your laptop.
k9.explain.pwd: pwd shows the folder you are in on this node.
k9.explain.cd: You moved to {dir} on this node.
k9.explain.ls: ls lists what is in that folder on the node.
k9.explain.read: You read part of the file.
k9.explain.grepNone: No line matched, so grep printed nothing.
k9.explain.echo: echo prints the words you give it.
k9.explain.export: export keeps that setting for the next commands in this shell.
k9.explain.mkdir: You made a new folder on the node.
k9.explain.rm: Gone. A node has no bin to undo this.
k9.explain.binaryFile: That file is not text. Read it with its own tool.
k9.explain.sedInPlace: sed -i changed {file} in place. Read it again to check.
k9.explain.sedPrint: sed printed the changed text. The file stays the same without -i.
k9.explain.help: These are the node commands you can practise here.
k9.explain.notInShell: {cmd}: the lesson shows what it does.
k9.explain.systemctlHelp: systemctl needs a command, like status, start or stop.
k9.explain.daemonReload: systemd read its unit files again. It prints nothing.
k9.explain.kubeletActive: The kubelet on {node} runs. It reports to the API server.
k9.explain.kubeletInactive: The kubelet on {node} is stopped. Start it with systemctl start kubelet.
k9.explain.kubeletEnabled: The kubelet starts when the node boots.
k9.explain.kubeletStop: The kubelet on {node} stopped. Pods keep running, but nobody reports them.
k9.explain.kubeletStart: The kubelet on {node} started. The node turns Ready soon.
k9.explain.kubeletRestart: The kubelet on {node} restarted. It printed nothing, like systemctl does.
k9.explain.containerdActive: containerd, the runtime under the kubelet, is running.
k9.explain.journal: These are the kubelet's own log lines, newest at the bottom.
k9.explain.journalFollow: journalctl -f keeps waiting for new lines. Press Ctrl+C to stop.
k9.explain.journalEmpty: The journal has nothing for {unit} on this node.
k9.explain.crictlPs: crictl asks containerd directly. It works even when the kubelet is down.
k9.explain.crictlPods: Each line is a pod sandbox on {node}.
k9.explain.crictlLogs: These are the logs of container {name} in pod {pod}.
k9.explain.crictlImages: These images are already on {node}. No download needed.
k9.explain.kubeadmVersion: This is the kubeadm on this node.
k9.explain.certsCheck: Leaf certificates last one year. The CAs last ten years.
k9.explain.certsRenewed: Renewed. Restart the control-plane pods so they load the new ones.
k9.explain.kubeadmUpgrade: Upgrade one minor version at a time. The lesson shows the plan.
k9.explain.kubeadmUpgradePlan: This is only a plan. Nothing changed yet. Upgrade the control plane first, then each node's kubelet.
k9.explain.etcdVersion: etcdctl talks to etcd. etcdutl works on its files.
k9.explain.etcdctlHelp: Give etcdctl a command, like snapshot save.
k9.explain.etcdctlSnapshotHelp: etcdctl snapshot only saves. etcdutl reads and restores snapshots.
k9.explain.etcdctlNoStatus: etcdctl 3.7 only saves snapshots. Use etcdutl snapshot status or restore.
k9.explain.etcdSaved: Saved: {file} holds the whole cluster at this moment.
k9.explain.etcdStatus: The snapshot's hash, revision, keys and size. It looks healthy.
k9.explain.etcdMembers: This cluster has one etcd member: the control-plane node.
k9.explain.etcdRestored: {dir} now holds the snapshot. Point etcd's data hostPath there.
k9.err.apiDown: Nothing answers at {server}. The API server or etcd is down.
k9.err.kubectlInNode: No kubeconfig on this node, so kubectl tries localhost:8080. Run kubectl on your laptop or on {node}.
k9.err.sshNoHost: No machine called {node} here. Check kubectl get nodes for names.
k9.err.sshUsage: Tell ssh which node: ssh dev-worker.
k9.err.dockerNoContainer: Docker has no container {node}. kind node names look like dev-worker.
k9.err.dockerExecUsage: Give a node and a command: docker exec -it dev-worker bash.
k9.err.notOnKind: kind nodes don't have {cmd}. The exam's nodes do.
k9.err.noEditorKind: kind nodes have no editor. Use sed -i 's/old/new/' FILE.
k9.err.noEtcdctlKind: kind nodes have no {cmd}. Run it in the etcd pod with kubectl exec.
k9.explain.noEditor: No full-screen editor here. Change a file with sed -i.
k9.err.unknownCmd: This node doesn't know {cmd}. Type help to see what works.
k9.err.noFile: {file} isn't there. Check the path with ls.
k9.err.noDir: That folder isn't there. Check the path with ls.
k9.err.catDir: {file} is a folder. Use ls to see inside.
k9.err.catUsage: Give a file name, like cat /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml.
k9.err.mvUsage: Give a source and a target: mv FILE FOLDER.
k9.err.cpDir: That is a folder. Copy folders with cp -r.
k9.err.rmDir: That is a folder. rm -r removes folders. Be careful.
k9.err.sedUsage: Give sed a script and a file: sed -i 's/old/new/' FILE.
k9.err.sedScript: sed couldn't read that script. Try 's/old/new/'.
k9.err.pipe: After | you can use grep, head or tail here.
k9.err.systemctlUnit: Name the service: systemctl status kubelet.
k9.err.noUnit: No service called {unit} here. The kubelet's is kubelet.
k9.err.crictlLogsUsage: Give a container ID from crictl ps -a.
k9.err.crictlNotFound: No container {id} here. Copy an ID from crictl ps -a.
k9.err.kubeadmWorker: Certificates live on the control-plane node, {node}.
k9.err.kubeadmRenewName: Renew one certificate by name, or all of them.
k9.err.etcdHang: etcdctl waits forever. It needs the etcd CA and a client certificate.
k9.err.etcdOpen: {file} isn't there. Check the certificate paths in etcd.yaml.
k9.err.etcdSaveUsage: Give one file name: snapshot save /opt/backup.db.
k9.err.etcdSaveDir: The folder for {file} isn't there. Make it with mkdir -p first.
k9.err.etcdctlRestore: etcdctl 3.7 can't restore. Use etcdutl --data-dir DIR snapshot restore FILE.
k9.err.etcdStatusUsage: Give the snapshot file: etcdutl snapshot status FILE.
k9.err.etcdRestoreUsage: Give the snapshot file and a new folder with --data-dir.
k9.err.etcdNoFile: {file} isn't there. Check where you saved the snapshot.
k9.err.etcdDirNotEmpty: {dir} already has data. Restore into a new, empty folder.
